payload.claim: For a ±10% Bitcoin grid bot with 20 levels (W≈0.20, δ≈1%, fee=0.1%) at 36% annualized volatility, the expected net monthly return on a random walk is approximately -0.5% of capital, equal to the fee cost.
payload.quote: Take a ±10% Bitcoin grid with 20 levels: W ≈ 0.20, δ ≈ 1%, f = 0.1%. At 36% annual volatility, daily σ is about 1.9%, so 30 days of squared moves add up to about 0.0107. The harvest is 0.0107 × C/2W (= 2.5) × 0.8 ≈ 2.1% of capital. On a random walk the expected cost is 0.0107 × 2.5 ≈ 2.7%. Net: about −0.5% a month, which is exactly the fees.

payload.text:
gauntlet-protocol-v6.1-intraday-daily-marks: intraday strategies are simulated per bar and measured on daily marks.

Rule. An intraday strategy (timeframe below 1d, session 24x7 only) is simulated bar by bar: vol-target sizing annualises with bars per year (365 x bars per day), short financing accrues per bar, the volatility-percentile regime window is 365 days of bars. Every statistic the gauntlet records or gates on is computed on the equity curve marked once per UTC day (the last bar of each date): the Sharpe floor's train Sharpe, the asset volatility that normalises edge per trade, the effective-trials clustering series, the deflated Sharpe and haircut inputs, the walk-forward folds and the regime labels, and the screen's recorded max drawdown. Trade-based gates (edge per trade, edge decay, Monte Carlo p05, ruin, cost stress) are unchanged. A daily strategy's bars are its daily marks, so every daily verdict before and after this note is computed identically.

Quarantine and the live gate. An intraday strategy's forward record is one quarantine_decision per cell per UTC day, written at the day's last bar: the cell is named ASSET@TF (for example BTCUSDT@1h) in the row's asset field and in that day's data snapshot; price, position and equity are the book at the day's last bar; the row adds entries and exits, the trades the strategy opened and closed that day. A UTC day with at least one bar is complete when the cell's last bar of the day is on disk, or when any later bar is; a UTC day with no bars at all is never recorded (a hole in the file). The live gate counts closed forward trades as the sum of exits over these rows, and a trading day for a 24x7 strategy is a UTC calendar day. Daily strategies' rows are unchanged.

crypto-grid-phase2-v1: Phase 2 of the chained crypto-grid-record-v1 grid is active from this entry: timeframes 1h, 4h and 12h on the same 76 assets, 228 cells. It adds no cell outside that grid, changes no existing verdict and re-judges nothing on the chain. Intraday statistics follow gauntlet-protocol-v6.1-intraday-daily-marks, chained just before this note.

THE CELLS. Phase 1's 76 cells (1d) were active from the grid record. With the 228 cells of this entry, 304 of the grid's 456 cells are active. The cells are the same 76 assets in the grid record's manifest order, each at 1h, 4h and 12h, and nothing else. Phase 3 (15m and 30m) stays inactive until its own Coen-gated commit.

THE EXCLUSION RULE. The grid record excludes a phase 2 cell whose own first bar falls after 2022-12-31. That rule was applied to every one of the 228 cells and excludes none, because every phase 2 cell's own first bar falls on or before 2022-12-31. The latest first bar of any phase 2 cell is APTUSDT, 2022-10-19. Every intraday price file starts no earlier than its asset's 1d file, so no cell's history reaches back past the history its asset was admitted on.

WHAT COUNTS. Each phase 2 cell is its own counted trial. Activating this phase adds its cells to what is searched. More registrations at a fixed bar is arithmetic about the denominator, never evidence of edge.

payload.claim: In China, the staggered introduction of ambient air quality monitoring in a city causes financial analysts based in that city to become substantially more likely to discuss air pollution in their coverage.
payload.quote: Exploiting the staggered rollout of China's ambient air quality monitoring program, we show that when monitoring is introduced in a city, analysts based there become substantially more likely to discuss air pollution.

source.title: Pollution Monitoring and the Pricing of Environmental Risk in Firms -- by Namrata Kala, Jalal Sani, Nemit Shroff, Pengdong Zhang

data_required: dates of city-level rollout of China's ambient air quality monitoring program
analyst report text/coverage data by analyst location and firm
classification of analyst location by city
testability.notes: Requires textual analysis of analyst reports to measure pollution discussion frequency.

payload.claim: Stock market reactions to analyst reports issued by analysts treated by the introduction of ambient air quality monitoring are more negative for brown firms, more positive for green firms, and largely unchanged for environmentally neutral firms, relative to reactions to reports from untreated analysts.
payload.quote: These changes in attention are reflected in stock prices: reports issued by treated analysts generate more negative market reactions for brown firms and more positive reactions for green firms, with little change for environmentally neutral firms.

source.title: Pollution Monitoring and the Pricing of Environmental Risk in Firms -- by Namrata Kala, Jalal Sani, Nemit Shroff, Pengdong Zhang

data_required: analyst report issuance dates and analyst location
stock price/return data around report dates
firm classification into brown/green/neutral based on environmental exposure
testability.notes: Core asset-pricing event-study claim distinguishing by firm environmental type.

payload.claim: The stock price reactions to reports issued by treated analysts regarding brown and green firms' environmental risk do not reverse in subsequent periods.
payload.quote: These price responses do not subsequently reverse.

source.title: Pollution Monitoring and the Pricing of Environmental Risk in Firms -- by Namrata Kala, Jalal Sani, Nemit Shroff, Pengdong Zhang

data_required: stock returns for brown/green firms following treated analyst reports
testability.notes: Tests for absence of mean-reversion in the price impact identified in the prior claim.

payload.claim: Following the introduction of ambient air quality monitoring in their city, analysts increase corporate site visits and issue less favorable assessments of brown firms and more favorable assessments of green firms compared to untreated analysts.
payload.quote: Treated analysts increase their information acquisition through corporate site visits and issue less favorable assessments of brown firms and more favorable assessments of green firms.

source.title: Pollution Monitoring and the Pricing of Environmental Risk in Firms -- by Namrata Kala, Jalal Sani, Nemit Shroff, Pengdong Zhang

data_required: analyst report favorability/rating data by firm type (brown/green)
testability.notes: Covers both information acquisition (site visits) and output (report favorability) channels.

payload.claim: In a month-by-maturity panel of U.S. Treasuries from 1988 to 2024, expected excess bond returns (measured using market yields and professional forecasts) have a 67% correlation with bonds' betas with respect to the stock market.
payload.quote: We measure expected excess returns using market yields and professional forecasts of future yields, showing that they are tightly linked to a standard measure of risk: bonds’ betas with respect to the stock market. In a month-by-maturity panel of U. S. Treasuries from 1988 to 2024, the correlation between expected excess returns and bond–stock betas is 67%.

source.title: Risk and Return in Government Bonds -- by Matteo Leombroni, Carolin Pflueger, Adi Sunderam

data_required: U.S. Treasury market yields by maturity 1988-2024
testability.notes: Decomposition claim relying on the same panel described in the preceding sentence.
